counterexamples: N(D(x)) and D(N(x)) are distinct tree-rule irreducibles and evaluate equally on every integer
lean_reference: BTCalculus.Rewrite.rewrite_N_D proves the integer identity; it is not a tree rule
notes: Refutes semantic canonicity of the smaller tree-rule set that omits N(D)→D(N). After that oriented commute, irreducibles are Pref∘D^k∘N^ε and inject into Z→Z (BTC-op-fragment-complete). Unique syntactic NF of either rule set is a different claim and is proved.
statement: Without N(D(x))→D(N(x)), tree-rule irreducibles of the operator fragment {D, I_a, S, N} are unique representatives of integer functions.
tested_range: exact identity N∘D = D∘N; probe set n in [-30, 30] in tests/unit/test_operator_fragment_nf.py
title: Operator-fragment tree NF is a unique semantic representative
